# Auto-Claim Automation Bridge

## Overview
HWA Helper dispatches RPC calls directly from the extension popup using a cleaned header set and a globally synchronized x-request-id counter, allowing mail rewards, battle reports, and completed quests to be claimed without manual game interaction.

## x-request-id Counter Synchronization
The game client (Unity) and the extension share the same RPC endpoint. The server rejects any request whose x-request-id is not strictly greater than the last accepted value. To prevent the 'Request id less than cached request id' HTTP 500 error:

- **intercept.js** maintains highestRequestId (an in-module integer) and mirrors it to sessionStorage('hwa_highest_request_id') so both the game's XHR and the extension's fetch calls share the same counter.
- On every outgoing game XHR, xhr.setRequestHeader is monkey-patched: if the game's candidate id is less than or equal to the current highest, the counter is incremented and the patched value is written instead.
- Extension-dispatched RPC calls use getNextRequestId(baseHeaders) which reads the sessionStorage mirror, increments, and then writes the new value back before returning.
- Observed game request ids are synced through the response interception path in intercept.js: the x-request-id from lastRpcHeaders is compared to highestRequestId and updates it if higher.

## Header Cleaning
Extension-dispatched RPC calls start from the last captured game request headers (lastRpcHeaders). Before re-using them:
1. Strip x-request-id and x-env-timestamp — these are regenerated fresh per dispatch.
2. Add x-request-id using getNextRequestId.
3. Copy remaining headers (authorization, x-platform, x-client-version, etc.) from the captured set to authenticate the dispatch as the same game session.

This avoids HTTP 500 errors caused by stale or duplicate header values.

## Pending Claim Detection (getPendingClaims)
getPendingClaims(cache) in popup-data.js inspects the current RPC cache snapshot and returns:
{ letterIds: [], hasReports: false, questIds: [], totalCount: 0 }
- letterIds: IDs of unclaimed mail letters.
- hasReports: true when battle reports are present and unclaimed.
- questIds: IDs of quests with completable status.
- totalCount: sum of all pending items.

## RPC Call Mapping (buildAutoClaimCalls)
buildAutoClaimCalls(cache, settings) in popup-data.js maps pending items to structured call objects:

| Setting | RPC method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| mail: true | mailFarm | Claim all unclaimed mail letters by ID |
| reports: true | readAndClaimAll | Mark and claim battle reports |
| quests: true | quest_multiFarm | Claim completed quests by ID |

Calls are dispatched sequentially in executeAutoClaim (popup.js): each call waits for its response before the next is sent. This prevents x-request-id collisions and avoids server-side duplicate claim errors.

## State Machine
autoClaimSettings (chrome.storage.local)
  loaded on popup open
currentAutoClaimSettings { mail, reports, quests, onOpen }
  renderAutoClaim(cache, settings) shows pending counts + badge
  user clicks 'Claim All' OR onOpen=true and !hasAutoClaimedThisSession
executeAutoClaim(cache, settings)
  buildAutoClaimCalls sequential RPC dispatch
  on success: unconditional api-record dispatch + optimistic cache refresh
  renderAutoClaim re-runs to clear counts

## Key Invariants
- Never dispatch if totalCount === 0.
- hasAutoClaimedThisSession (module-level boolean) prevents repeated auto-runs during the same popup session when onOpen is true.
- After dispatch, optimistically refresh popup cache and re-render without waiting for a full RPC snapshot.

## Source Provenance
- @task-VHE-H817RH (initial auto-claim implementation)
- @task-VHE-VXZJZG (HTTP 500 fix: header cleaning + sequential dispatch)
- @task-VHE-PJJD5V (x-request-id sync + optimistic UI update)

## Dispatch Rules

All helper RPC dispatch inherits @doc/architecture/shared-rpc-settings. The shared enable switch is false by default; `socketRefreshMode` selects Piggyback by default or explicit Direct for every feature.
